o: Když kapitán van Toch toto vypravoval, zježily se mu vlasy v týle úchvatem a vzrušením.
t: As Captain van Toch was saying this, the hair on the back of his neck stood up with horror and excitement.

o: „Ja, pane, to teda jsem přisahal.
t: "Yes, sir, that I did swear.

o: Od ty doby, chlapče, jsem neměl chvílu pokoje.
t: Since then, boy, I haven't had a moment's peace.

o: V Padang jsem vzal svy prázdniny a poslal jsem tem židům v Amsterdam sto padesát sedum perel, všecko, co mně ty my zvířátka donesly.
t: In Padang I took my leave and sent those Jews in Amsterdam a hundred and fifty-seven pearls — everything those beasts of mine brought me.

o: Potom jsem našel takovyho jednoho chlapa, on to byl Dajak a shark-killer, co zabíjí ty žraloky nožem ve vodě.
t: Then I found a certain fellow, a Dayak and a shark-killer, a man who kills sharks with a knife in the water.

o: Hrozné zloděj a vrah, ten Dajak.
t: A dreadful thief and murderer, that Dayak.

o: A s ním po takovy maly tramp-lodi zpátky na Tana Masa, a teď, fella, tu budeš tym svym nožem zabíjet ty žraloky.
t: And with him, on a small tramp steamer, back to Tana Masa; and now, fella, you'll be killing those sharks with your knife.

o: Já chcel, aby tam ty sharks vybil, aby dali pokoj mým ještěrkům.
t: I wanted him to clear out those sharks, so they'd leave my lizards alone.

o: On byl takové vrah a pohan, ten Dajak, že si nic nedělal ani z těch tapa-boys.
t: That Dayak was such a murderer and heathen that he didn't care about the tapa-boys either.

o: Čert nečert, jemu to bylo jedno.
t: Devil take it, he didn't care in the slightest.

o: A já jsem zatím dělal na těch lizards svy observations a experiments, – tož počkat, já o tom mám takovou lodní knihu, do ktery jsem to každé den psal.“
t: And meanwhile I was making my observations and experiments on the lizards — well, wait, I have such a ship's logbook that I wrote all of it down every day."

o: Kapitán vytáhl z náprsní kapsy objemný notes, ve kterém počal listovat.
t: The captain pulled a bulky notebook out of his breast pocket and began to leaf through it.

o: „Tož kteryho dnes máme?
t: "Well, which one have we got today?

o: Pravda, dvacátyho pátyho června.
t: Right, the twenty-fifth of June.

o: Tak například dvacáty páty červen, to bylo teda loni.
t: For example, the twenty-fifth of June — that was last year, then.

o: Ja, tady. Dajak zabil žraloka.
t: Yes, here. The Dayak killed a shark.

o: Lizards mají ohromné interest o tu mrchu.
t: The lizards have an enormous interest in that carcass.

o: Toby – to byl teda jeden takové menší ještěrka, ale tuze chytré,“ vysvětloval kapitán.
t: “Toby – well, he was one of the smaller lizards, but a very clever one,” the captain explained.

o: „Já jim musel dát všelijaky jmena, víš? abych o nich mohl psát tu knihu.
t: “I had to give them all sorts of names, you know, so that I could write about them in that book.”

o: – Tož Toby strkal prsty do ty díry od toho nože.
t: – So Toby was sticking his fingers into that hole made by the knife.

o: Večer nosili suchy větve na můj oheň.
t: In the evening they brought dry branches to my fire.

o: – To nic není,“ bručel kapitán.
t: – That’s nothing,” the captain muttered.

o: „Já najdu nějaké jiné den.
t: “I’ll find some other day.

o: Třeba dvacátyho června, ne?
t: Maybe the twentieth of June, eh?

o: – Lizards stavěli dál ten – ten – jak se řekne jetty?“
t: – The lizards went on building that – that – what do you call it, a jetty?”

o: „Ja, hráz. Takové dam.
t: “Yes, a weir. A dam like that.

o: Teda stavěli dál ten nové hráz na severozápadním konci Devil Bay.
t: So they went on building that new weir at the northwest end of Devil Bay.

o: – Člověče,“ vysvětloval, „to ti bylo báječny dílo.
t: – Man,” he explained, “that was a magnificent piece of work.

o: Hotové breakwater.“
t: A proper breakwater.”

o: „Ja. Oni na ty straně snášeli svy vajíčka a chceli tam mít tichou vodu, víš?
t: “Yes. On that side they laid their eggs and they wanted still water there, you know?

o: To oni si sami vymysleli, že tam udělají takové ten dam; ale já tě řeknu, že by žádné úředník nebo inžinýr od Waterstaat v Amsterdam neudělal lepší plán na takové podvodní hráz.
t: It was their own idea to make such a dam there; but I’ll tell you, no official or engineer from the Waterstaat in Amsterdam would have drawn a better plan for such an underwater weir.

o: Náramně šikovny dílo, jenomže jim to brala voda.
t: A remarkably skillful job, only the water kept washing it away.

o: Oni si vyhrabávají pod vodou aji takovy hluboky díry do břehů, a v těch dírách oni ve dne žijou.
t: They dig themselves deep holes in the banks under the water, and they live in those holes by day.

o: Hrozně chytry zvířata, pane, docela jako beavers.“
t: Frightfully clever creatures, sir, quite like beavers.”

o: „Ja, ty veliky myši, co dovedou stavět ty přehrady na řece.
t: “Yes, those big mice that can build those dams on the river.

o: Oni tam měli spoustu těch hrází a hráziček, v tom Devil Bay, takovy krásně rovny dams, že to vypadalo jako nějaky město.
t: They had heaps of those weirs and little dams there in Devil Bay, such beautifully level dams, that it looked like some town.

o: A nakonec chceli postavit ten hráz přes cely ten Devil Bay.
t: And in the end they wanted to build a weir right across the whole of Devil Bay.

o: Tož tak. – Už dovedou odvalovat kameny heverama,“ četl dále.
t: So it is. – They can already lever the stones off now," he read on.

o: „Albertovi – to byl jeden tapa-boy – to rozmačkalo dva prsty.
t: "Albert – he was a tapa-boy – that crushed two fingers.

o: – Dvacátyho prvního: Dajak sežral Alberta!
t: – On the twentieth of the first: Somebody ate Albert!

o: Ale bylo mu po něm špatně.
t: But he felt badly about it afterwards.

o: Patnáct kapek opia.
t: Fifteen drops of opium.

o: Slíbil, že už to neudělá.
t: He promised he wouldn't do it again.

o: Pršelo celé den.
t: It rained all day.

o: – Třicátyho června: Lizards stavěli ten hráz.
t: – On the thirtieth of June: The Lizards were building that dam.

o: Toby nechce dělat.
t: Toby doesn't want to work.

o: – Pane, ten byl chytré,“ vysvětloval kapitán s obdivem.
t: – Sir, that one was clever," the captain explained admiringly.

o: „Ty chytry nikdy nechcou nic dělat.
t: "The clever ones never want to do anything.

o: On furt něco kutil, ten Toby.
t: That Toby was always fiddling with something.

o: Co je to platny, i mezi ještěrkama jsou tuze velky rozdíly.
t: What's the point – even among the lizards there are great differences.

o: – Třetího července: Sergeant dostal nůž.
t: – On the third of July: Sergeant got a knife.

o: – To byl takové veliké, silné ještěrka, ten Sergeant.
t: – That was a big, strong lizard, that Sergeant.

o: A moc šikovné, pane.
t: And very clever, sir.

o: – Sedmyho července: Sergeant zabil tym nožem jeden cuttle-fish – to je taková ryba, co má v sobě ty hnědy sračky, víš?“
t: – On the seventh of July: Sergeant killed a cuttlefish with that knife – that's a fish with brown guts inside, you know?

o: – Desátyho července: Sergeant zabil tym nožem jeden veliké jelly-fish – to je taková potvora jako sulc, a pálí jako kopřiva.
t: – On the tenth of July: Sergeant killed a big jellyfish with that knife – it's a monster like a stingray, and it stings like a nettle.

o: Šeredny zvíře to je.
t: It's a nasty beast.

o: – A teď pozor, pane Bondy.
t: – And now watch, Mr Bond.

o: Třináctyho července.
t: July thirteenth.

o: Já to tu mám podtrženo.
t: I've got it underlined here.

o: Sergeant zabil tym nožem malyho žraloka.
t: The Sergeant killed a small shark with that knife.

o: Váha sedumdesát liber.
t: Seventy pounds' weight.

o: – Tak tady to je, pane Bondy,“ prohlásil kapitán J. van Toch slavnostně.
t: “Here it is, Mr Bond,” declared Captain J. van Toch solemnly.

o: „Tady to stojí černy na bílym.
t: “It's here in black and white.

o: To je ten veliké den, chlapče.
t: That's the great day, boy.

o: Akorát třináctyho července loni.“
t: Just on the thirteenth of July last year.”

o: Kapitán zavřel notes.
t: The captain closed the notebook.

o: „Já se za to nestydím, pane Bondy: já jsem tam na břehu toho Devil Bay klek na kolena a brečel od samy čisty radosti.
t: “I'm not ashamed of it, Mr Bond: I was there on the shore of that Devil Bay, kneeling and weeping with sheer joy.

o: Teď už jsem věděl, že se ty my tapa-boys nedají.
t: By then I already knew that my tapa-boys wouldn't let themselves be pushed around.

o: Ten Sergeant za to dostal krásny novy harpun – harpun máš to nejlepší, chlapče, když budeš lovit žraloky –, a já mu povídám, be a man, Sergeant, a ukaž tem tapa-boys, že se možou bránit.
t: The Sergeant got a fine new harpoon for it – a harpoon is the best thing you've got, boy, when you're hunting sharks – and I told him, be a man, Sergeant, and show those tapa-boys that they can defend themselves.

o: Člověče,“ křikl kapitán, vyskočil a bouchal nadšením do stolu, „víš, že tam za tři dny plaval ohromné chcíplé žralok, full of gashes, jak se to řekne?“
t: “Man,” the captain shouted, jumping up and thumping the table with enthusiasm, “do you know that in three days an enormous bloody shark swam there, full of gashes, as you put it?”

o: „Ja, samá díra od toho harpunu.“
t: “Yes, one hole right through from that harpoon.”

o: Kapitán se napil, až to klokotalo.
t: The captain drank until it gurgled.

o: „Tož tak je to, pane Bondy.
t: “So that's how it is, Mr Bond.

o: Teď teprve jsem udělal s tema tapa-boys… takové jako kontrakt.
t: Only then did I make a contract with those tapa-boys…

o: Totiž dal jsem jako svy slovo, že když mně donesou ty perlovy škeble, že já jim za to dám ty harpoons a knives, jako ty nože, aby se mohli bránit, see?
t: That is, I gave my word that when they brought me those pearl shells, I would give them the harpoons and knives, those knives, so that they could defend themselves, see?

o: To je poctivé business, pane.
t: That's honest business, sir.

o: Co je to platny, člověk má byt poctivé i k tem zvířatům.
t: What's the point of it – a man has to be honest even towards animals.

o: A taky nějaky dřevo jsem jim dal.
t: And I gave them some wood too.

o: A dva železny wheelbarrows –“
t: And two iron wheelbarrows—

o: „Trakaře. Kolečka.“
t: “Wheelbarrows. Little wheels.”

o: „Ja. Takovy kolečka.
t: “Yes. Little wheels like that.

o: Aby mohli vozit ty kameny na ten hráz.
t: So they could haul those stones up to that dam.

o: Oni to, chudáci, museli všechno tahat v tech svych tlapičkách, víš?
t: They, poor devils, had to drag everything in those little feet of theirs, you know?

o: No, hrůzu věcí dostali.
t: Well, they got a positively monstrous haul of things.

o: Já bych je nechcel ošidit, to zase ne.
t: I wouldn't cheat them, that's for sure.

o: Počkej, chlapče, něco ti ukážu.“
t: “Wait, boy, I'll show you something.”

o: Kapitán van Toch si nadzvedl jednou rukou břicho a druhou vylovil z kapsy u kalhot plátěný pytlík.
t: Captain van Toch hitched up his belly with one hand and with the other fished a canvas bag out of his trouser pocket.

o: „Tož tady to mám,“ řekl a vysypal jeho obsah na stůl.
t: “Here it is,” he said, and tipped its contents out onto the table.

o: Bylo to na tisíc perel všech velikostí: drobné jako semenec, větší, veliké jako hrách, několik ve velikosti třešně; dokonalé perly kapkovité, hrbolaté perly barokní, perly stříbřité, modré, pleťově nažloutlé, naběhlé do černa i růžové.
t: There were a thousand pearls of all sizes: tiny ones like a seed, bigger ones, large ones like a pea, several the size of a cherry; flawless teardrop pearls, knobbly baroque pearls, pearls silvery, blue, sallow-yellow, flushed with black and pink.

o: G. H. Bondy byl jako u vidění; nemohl si pomoci, musel se v nich přehrabovat, válet je konečky prstů, přikrývat oběma dlaněmi –.
t: G. H. Bondy was as if in a trance; he could not help himself, he had to rummage through them, roll them between his fingertips, cover them with both palms—.

o: „To je krása,“ vydechl s úžasem, „kapitáne, to je jako sen!“
t: “This is beauty,” he breathed in wonder, “Captain, this is like a dream!”

o: „Ja,“ děl kapitán nevzrušeně.
t: “Yes,” the captain said, unperturbed.

o: A tech žraloků zabili asi třicet za ten rok, co jsem tam s nima byl.
t: And they killed about thirty of those sharks in the year I was there with them.

o: Mám to tady napsany,“ řekl ťukaje na náprsní kapsu.
t: I have it written down here,” he said, tapping his breast pocket.

o: „Však co tech nožů jsem já jim dal, a pět tech harpoons – Mně přijdou ty nože skoro na dva americky dollars apiece, tož teda za kus.
t: “But all those knives I gave them, and five of those harpoons—those knives come to almost two American dollars apiece, so, per piece.

o: Moc dobry nože, chlapce, z takovy ty ocele, co nechytá žádné rust.“
t: Very good knives, boy, made of a steel that catches no rust.”

o: „Ja. Protože to mají byt podvodní nože, jako do moře.
t: “Yes. Because they have to be underwater knives, like for the sea.”

o: A ty Batakové taky stáli hrůzu peněz.“
t: And you Bataks are afraid of money too."

o: „Jací Batakové?“
t: "What Bataks?"

o: „Tož ty domorodci na tom ostrově.
t: "Well, the natives there on the island.

o: Oni mají takovou víru, že ty tapa-boys jsou jako čerti, a hrozně se jich bojí.
t: They have such a belief that those tapa-boys are like devils, and they fear them terribly.

o: A když viděli, že já s tema jejich čerty mluvím, tak mě chceli dočista zabít.
t: And when they saw me talking with their devils, they wanted to kill me outright.

o: Po cely noci tloukli do takovych zvonů, aby ty čerty jako zahnali od toho svyho kampongu.
t: All night long they banged on such bells, to drive those devils away from their kampong.

o: Hrozné rámus dělali, pane.
t: They made a terrible racket, sir.

o: A pak vždycky ráno na mně chceli, abych jim za to zvonění zaplatil.
t: And then every morning they wanted me to pay them for the ringing.

o: Za tu prácu, co s tím měli, víš?
t: For the work they had with it, you know?

o: Tož co je to platny, ty Batakove jsou moc veliky zloději.
t: Well, what's the use, those Bataks are great thieves.

o: Ale s tema tapa-boys, sir, s tema ještěrkama by se dal dělat poctivé business.
t: But with those tapa-boys, sir, with those lizards, one could do honest business.

o: Tož tak. Moc dobré kšeft, pane Bondy.“
t: Well, that's so. Very good business, Mr. Bondy."

o: G. H. Bondy si připadal jako v pohádce.
t: G. H. Bondy felt as though he were in a fairy tale.

o: „Kupovat od nich perly?“
t: "Buying pearls from them?"

o: „Ja. Jenže v Devil Bay už žádny perly nejsou, a na jinych ostrovech nejsou žádny tapa-boys.
t: "Yes. Only there are no pearls left in Devil Bay, and on the other islands there are no tapa-boys.

o: To je ta celá věc, mládenče.“
t: That's the whole point, young man."

o: Kapitán J. van Toch vítězně nadul tváře.
t: Captain J. van Toch puffed out his cheeks triumphantly.

o: „To je právě ten veliké kšeft, co já jsem vymyslel ve svy hlavě.
t: "That's exactly the big business I thought up in my own head.

o: Chlapče,“ řekl bodaje do vzduchu tlustým prstem, „vždyť ono tech ještěrků náramně přibylo od tý doby, co já jsem se jich ujal!
t: Boy," said the fat man, pointing into the air with a thick finger, "the number of those lizards has grown mightily since I took them in hand!

o: Oni se teď možou bránit, you see?
t: They can defend themselves now, you see?"

o: Eh? A furt jich bude víc!
t: Eh? And there'll be more of them all the time!

o: No tak, pane Bondy?
t: Well, Mr Bondy?

o: Nebyl by to báječné podnik?“
t: Wouldn't that be a splendid enterprise?

o: „Já pořád nevidím,“ děl G. H. Bondy nejistě, „… jak to vlastně myslíte, kapitáne?“
t: "I still don't see," said G. H. Bondy uncertainly, "... what do you mean, captain?"

o: „Tož vozit ty tapa-boys na jiny perlovy ostrovy,“ vyrazilo to konečně z kapitána.
t: "Well, carrying these tapa-boys off to other pearl islands," the captain finally got out.

o: „Já jsem vypozoroval, že ty ještěrkove se nemožou sami dostat přes volny a hluboky moře.
t: "I've noticed that these lizard folk can't get across the open sea and deep water by themselves.

o: Oni dovedou chvílu plavat a chvílu ťapkat po dně, ale ve veliky hloubce, tam je na ně moc veliké tlak; oni jsou tuze měkký, víš?
t: They can swim a while and wade along the bottom for a while, but at great depth the pressure on them is too much; they're very soft, you know?

o: Ale kdybych já měl takovou loď, co by se v ní dal pro ně udělat takové tank, takové nádrž na vodu, tož bych já je mohl rozvážet, kam bych chcel, see?
t: But if I had a ship where one could make such tanks for them, such water tanks, then I could carry them wherever I wanted, see?

o: A oni by tam hledali perle, a já bych za nima jezdil a dovážel jim ty nože a harpoons a jiny takovy věci, co oni potřebujou.
t: And they would look for pearls there, and I would go about after them and bring them the knives and harpoons and other such things as they need.

o: Ty chudáčkove se v tom Devil Bay tak roz – rozprasili, ne?“
t: Those poor fellows have spread out so in that Devil Bay, haven't they?

o: „Ja, rozmnožili, že už tam nebudou mět co žrát.
t: "Yes, they've multiplied so that there won't be anything left for them to eat there.

o: Oni žerou, co jsou ty menší rybičky a molluscs a takové ten vodní hmyz; ale aji brambory oni možou žrat a suchary a takovy obyčejny věci.
t: They eat the smaller fish and molluscs and such water insects; but they can also eat potatoes and biscuits and other ordinary things.

o: Tož to by šlo je krmit v takovych tanks na lodi.
t: So they could be fed in such tanks on the ship.

o: A já bych je na šikovnych místech, kde není moc lidí, pustil zase do vody a udělal tam takovy – takovy farms pro ty my ještěrky.
t: And I would set them loose again in the water at suitable places, where there aren't many people, and set up there such – such farms for our little lizards.

o: Tož já bych chcel, aby se mohli uživit, ty zvířátka.
t: So I would want them to be able to feed, the little animals.

o: Oni jsou moc mily a chytry, pane Bondy.
t: They are very nice and clever, Mr Bondy.

o: Však až je uvidíš, chlapče, tak řekneš Hullo, Captain, to máš užitečny zvířátka.
t: But once you see them, my boy, you'll say 'Hello, Captain' – that's a useful animal you have.

o: Ja. On: teď jsou lidi cely blázni po perlách, pane Bondy.
t: Yes. Now people are all mad about pearls, Mr Bondy.

o: Tož to je ten veliké business, co jsem já vymyslel.“
t: So that's the great business I invented."

o: G. H. Bondy byl na rozpacích.
t: G. H. Bondy was in two minds.

o: „Je mně hrozně líto, kapitáne,“ začal váhavě, „ale – já opravdu nevím –“
t: "I'm terribly sorry, Captain," he began hesitantly, "but— I really don't know—"

o: Blankytné oči kapitána J. van Tocha se zalily slzami.
t: The blue eyes of Captain J. van Toch filled with tears.

o: „Tož to je špatny, chlapče.
t: "Well, that's bad, my boy."

o: Já bych ti tady nechal ty všecky perly jako… jako guaranty na tu loď, ale tu loď já sám koupit nemožu.
t: I'd leave you all those pearls here as... as security for the ship, but I can't buy the ship myself.

o: Já bych věděl o moc šikovny lodi tuhle v Rotterdam… ona je na Diesel motor –“
t: I know of a very smart ship here in Rotterdam... she's got a Diesel engine—"

o: „Proč jste ten obchod nenavrhl někomu v Holandsku?“
t: "Why didn't you propose the deal to someone in Holland?"

o: Kapitán zavrtěl hlavou.
t: The captain shook his head.

o: „Ty lidi já znám, chlapče.
t: "I know those people, my boy."

o: S tema já o tom mluvit nemožu.
t: "I can't talk to them about that."

o: Tož já bych třeba,“ řekl zamyšleně, „vozil s tou lodí aji jiny věci, všechny možny goods, pane, a prodával bych je po tech ostrovech.
t: "Well, for instance," he said thoughtfully, "I'd carry other goods in that ship too, all sorts of goods, sir, and sell them around those islands."

o: Ja, to bych já mohl.
t: Yes, I could do that.

o: Já tam mám hrozně moc známostí, pane Bondy.
t: "I have an enormous number of contacts there, Mr. Bondy."

o: Přitom bych mohl mět v ty my lodi takové tanks na ty my ještěrky –“
t: "And I could put tanks in my ships for those lizards of yours—"

o: „O tom by se dalo spíš uvažovat,“ přemítal G. H. Bondy.
t: "That is more worth considering," G. H. Bondy mused.

o: Nu ano, musíme hledat nové trhy pro náš průmysl.
t: "Well, we have to find new markets for our industry."

o: Náhodou jsem o tom mluvil nedávno s několika lidmi – Já bych chtěl koupit jednu nebo dvě lodi, jednu pro Jižní Ameriku a druhou pro ty východní končiny –“
t: "As it happens, I was talking about it recently with a few people— I'd like to buy one or two ships, one for South America and another for the eastern regions—"

o: „To tě chválím, pane Bondy, sir.
t: "I commend you for that, Mr. Bondy, sir."

o: Lodě jsou teď hrozně laciny, možeš jich koupit plné přístav –“ Kapitán van Toch se pustil do technického výkladu, kde a zač jsou na prodej jaké vessels a boats a tank-steamers; G. H. Bondy ho neposlouchal a jen ho pozoroval; G. H. Bondy se vyznal v lidech.
